summary: The payment failures in INC-012 were caused by capacity exhaustion of the shared ledger-db: its disk filled from 89.4% (13:00Z) to 100% by 14:58Z, and PostgreSQL could no longer write WAL or extend data files, so all write-heavy users of that datastore began failing their writes (H2, confidence 0.72, medium). The payment-service v6.0.0 mandate flow (dep-6203) is coincidental: ledger-db was already 95% full at 14:15:45Z and ~98% at the 14:46Z deploy, a writer that never received v6.0.0 (order-service) emits the identical ENOSPC signature, and the 15:12Z rollback produced no recovery in any writer through 16:57Z. The dominant error everywhere is 'No space left on device', not a validation or unknown-entry-type rejection (H1/H3 rejected at 0.02 each). Residual uncertainty is limited to the exact space consumer — WAL retained by the inactive 'analytics_cdc' replication slot is strongly indicated by recurring ledger-db WARNs and the exact HIST-114 precedent, but no per-slot byte metric exists to prove it — and the uncharacterised settlement-service error signature.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Shared ledger-db disk exhaustion from WAL retained by an inactive replication slot — all write-heavy writers fail
ranked_hypotheses.statement: ledger-db's filesystem filled steadily during the morning (89.4% at 13:00Z -> 100% by 14:58Z) while an inactive replication slot 'analytics_cdc' retained ~78 GB of WAL, and the retained WAL is the dominant space consumer. PostgreSQL reached 100% disk and could no longer write WAL or extend data files, so every write-heavy client of the shared ledger-db (payment-service, order-service, settlement-service) began failing its DB writes at ~14:54-15:01Z, surfacing as ~48-62% error rates. No faulty deployment is required, and the payment-service v6.0.0 rollout is coincidental.

causal_chain.claim: Inactive replication slot 'analytics_cdc' retains 78423 MB of WAL, warned from 14:16:25Z onward (5 occurrences)

ledger-db disk_used_pct rises monotonically 89.39% (13:00Z) -> >95% by ~14:05-14:10Z -> 98%+ from the 14:38Z bucket -> 100.0% first reached in the 14:58Z bucket, then pins at exactly 100 through 16:55Z with no recovery

PostgreSQL can no longer write: WARN 'disk usage 95%' 14:15:45Z / 'disk usage 98%' 14:48:20Z, then hard failures PANIC 'could not write to file pg_wal/xlogtemp...: No space left on device' from 15:01:01Z (153x) and 'could not extend file base/16402/2619: No space left on device' from 15:01:39Z (139x)

Replication lag ramps in lockstep with the fill (2468ms at 13:00Z -> 5227ms at 16:45Z) while cpu_pct stays flat ~30% and connections_active stays flat ~61-63 — space/IO-bound, not compute- or connection-bound

payment-service ledger writes fail: 88 of 89 matched WARN+ lines are 'ledger write failed: ERROR: could not extend file: No space left on device', first at 15:00:26Z; error rate jumps 0.2% -> 61.52% between the 14:55 and 15:00 buckets

Non-v6.0.0 writers fail the same way: order-service emits 238 WARN+ lines in 14:45-16:59Z dominated by 'INSERT INTO orders failed: No space left on device' (236, first 15:00:42Z), and its error rate jumps to 16.17% avg / 49.57% max in the 14:54Z bucket, holding ~47-48% through 16:51Z
settlement-service, also a non-v6.0.0 ledger-db writer, degrades simultaneously: 18.07% avg / 54.52% max at 14:54Z, holding ~54-56% through 16:51Z

All three writers break in the same minutes (payment 15:00:26Z, order 15:00:42Z, ledger-db PANIC 15:01:01Z), consistent with one shared component crossing the ENOSPC threshold rather than each writer's own change

Blast radius is selective because only writers that actually issue failing disk writes degrade: portfolio-service (flat ~0.2%, one unrelated connection-reset retry log) shows normal traffic (~570 req/s) and normal DB pool usage (~12 connections) all window

The rollout is not the trigger: v6.0.0 deployed 14:46Z while ledger-db was already at ~98% disk and order/settlement 5xx had already begun at 14:54Z; the only change in the window and in the whole 12-day lookback is dep-6203, and its 15:12Z rollback produces no recovery (payment stays 58-70%, order ~47-49%, settlement ~53-58% through 16:57Z)

Exact historical precedent for the mechanism: HIST-114 (2025-04-18, ledger-db) 'disk full from retained WAL', root cause 'Inactive replication slot retained WAL until disk filled', resolution 'Dropped slot; added slot-lag alert'

assumptions: The retained WAL from the inactive 'analytics_cdc' slot is the dominant space consumer. The disk fill ramp is now measured (F19/F20) and matches the WAL-retention warnings, but no metric exposes WAL bytes or free bytes, so the causal direction (consumer stopped -> WAL retained -> disk fill) versus (something else filled the disk while the slot warning was incidental) is still an inference supported mainly by the exact HIST-114 precedent (F35).

settlement-service fails via the same disk-exhaustion mechanism. Its ~54-56% error rate is confirmed (F14/F23) but it emitted ZERO WARN+ logs in both 14:45-16:59Z and 11:00-16:59Z (F27), so its error signature is genuinely unknown; it is inferred from being a co-writer of the same disk-full datastore.

The slot's consumer stall began before 14:16:25Z. The consumer is unmodeled (not in topology, no telemetry, F33/F34), so its stall time cannot be pinned; the direction of causality is asserted from the HIST-114 precedent, not observed.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Shared-dependency failure surfaced first on payment-service, with retry/circuit-breaker amplification inflating its error rate
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The origin is a degraded shared dependency (ledger-db storage); payment-service's headline ~61% error rate is partially inflated by retries / circuit breaking so that payment-service looks worse than the true write-failure share, and the reporter's attention was drawn to the newest high-volume writer.

causal_chain.claim: ledger-db storage saturates and write calls fail
payment-service retries or circuit-breaks on those failures, so its reported error_rate overstates the fraction of genuinely failed user requests
payment-service error rate reads 61.52%, higher than the co-writer order-service (~48%) and comparable to settlement-service (~55%)
payment request rate is flat (~100 req/s) across the window, so the jump is not load-driven and the amplification must come from retry/breaker behaviour rather than volume

assumptions: Retry or circuit-breaker amplification exists in payment-service and is not itself the fault (no log or metric evidence of retry counts was produced)
The ~13-point gap between payment-service (~62%) and order-service (~48%) reflects amplification rather than a different mix of endpoints or a different write:read ratio

ranked_hypotheses.title: An unrecorded change or unmodeled actor triggered/vaccelerated the ledger-db disk fill; the v6.0.0 correlation is coincidental
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The disk fill was started or accelerated by something outside the recorded change set — an unrecorded config/flag change, a cron/batch job, or an unmodeled component (e.g. the CDC/analytics consumer or a log-retention rotation) — and payment-service v6.0.0's 14:46Z deploy merely coincided with it.

causal_chain.claim: An unrecorded change or unmodeled actor between ~13:00Z and 14:15Z accelerated ledger-db disk consumption
ledger-db crosses 95% at ~14:05-14:10Z and 98% from the 14:38Z bucket, reaching 100% by 14:58Z
Writers fail from 14:54Z (order/settlement) and 15:00Z (payment) onward

assumptions: A real change exists that neither the deployment tool nor the config/flag tool recorded — the disk-fill trigger is not uniquely tied to the WAL/slot story, since the slot-stall timing is inferred rather than observed
The exact HIST-114 precedent (same datastore, same symptom, same resolution) coincidentally matches an unrelated fill cause

ranked_hypotheses.title: payment-service v6.0.0 mandate flow wrote a new ledger entry type that the ledger rejected
ranked_hypotheses.statement: Reporter's original theory: the v6.0.0 mandate flow writes MANDATE_HOLD entries that ledger-db rejects, so mandate ledger writes fail and payment-service error rate jumps to ~60%.

causal_chain.claim: payment-service v6.0.0 (dep-6203) deployed 14:46Z introducing ledger entry type MANDATE_HOLD
ledger-db lacks schema/constraint support for MANDATE_HOLD
MANDATE_HOLD writes fail with a validation/unknown-entry-type error
error rate jumps to ~61%

ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Contradicted on mechanism, scope and timing. Mechanism: the dominant payment-service error is 'ERROR: could not extend file: No space left on device' (F8), not a validation/unknown-entry-type error, and the mandate-substring log query returned 0 matches. Timing: ledger-db was already 95% full at 14:15:45Z and ~98% at deploy time 14:46Z (F10, F17, F20), and the fill began before any mandate traffic could matter. Scope: writers that never received v6.0.0 fail identically — order-service emits the same no-space error (F25, F13) and settlement-service degrades to ~55% (F14). Reversibility: the 15:12Z rollback of dep-6203 produces no recovery in any writer through 16:57Z (F21, F22, F23).

ranked_hypotheses.title: Version skew: MANDATE_HOLD requires a ledger-db schema/config change that was never deployed
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The new ledger entry type in v6.0.0 requires a ledger-db schema or config change (CHECK constraint, enum value, column) that was never deployed, so MANDATE_HOLD writes fail while legacy writes succeed.

causal_chain.claim: v6.0.0 introduces MANDATE_HOLD (dep-6203)
No corresponding ledger-db schema/constraint change was deployed
MANDATE_HOLD writes fail while legacy writes succeed

ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Same origin family (the new entry type) and same mechanism/scope objections as H1: the observed failures are disk-exhaustion errors on a shared datastore (F8, F10, F25) affecting a writer that never wrote MANDATE_HOLD (order-service, F13/F25). Additionally the 'no ledger-side change' premise is now weaker in the opposite direction: the 12-day deployment query returns only dep-6203 and the config-change query over 2026-05-20..06-01 returns count 0 (F31, F32), so nothing ledger-side was deployed or flagged — but nothing ledger-side needed to be, since the failure is capacity, not schema.

facts.statement: The shared ledger-db filesystem filled monotonically from 89.39% at 13:00Z to 99.92%/100% by the 14:55Z bucket, and then pinned at exactly 100% for every bucket from 15:00Z through 16:55Z with no recovery or cleanup.
ledger-db crossed critical thresholds before the v6.0.0 rollout completed: >95% by ~14:05-14:10Z, 98%+ from the 14:38Z bucket, and 100% first in the 14:58Z bucket; the deploy occurred at 14:46Z.

ledger-db emitted 'disk usage 95%' at 14:15:45Z and 'disk usage 98%' at 14:48:20Z, followed by hard write failures: PANIC 'could not write to file "pg_wal/xlogtemp...": No space left on device' first at 15:01:01Z (153 occurrences) and 'could not extend file "base/16402/2619": No space left on device' first at 15:01:39Z (139 occurrences).

The dominant payment-service error signature is a disk-write failure, not a validation/unknown-entry-type error: 88 of 89 matched WARN+ logs are 'ledger write failed: ERROR: could not extend file: No space left on device', first seen 15:00:26Z.

order-service — a ledger-db writer that did NOT receive v6.0.0 — emits the same ENOSPC signature: 238 WARN+ logs in 14:45-16:59Z, dominated by 'INSERT INTO orders failed: No space left on device' (count 236, first_seen 15:00:42Z, last_match 16:57:47Z).

Non-v6.0.0 ledger-db writers degraded in the same minute as payment-service: order-service jumped from ~0.2% to 16.17% avg / 49.57% max in the 14:54Z bucket, and settlement-service from ~0.2% to 18.07% avg / 54.52% max in the same bucket; both held ~47-56% through 16:51Z.

DECISIVE NEGATIVE: no writer recovers after the 15:12Z rollback of dep-6203 — payment-service stays in the 58-70% band through 16:57Z, order-service at ~47-50%, settlement-service at 53-58%, all simultaneously elevated at the end of data.

The only change in the incident window across all services is payment-service v6.0.0 (dep-6203), deployed 14:46Z, rolled back 15:12Z; a 12-day lookback returns exactly one deployment (dep-6203) and zero config/feature-flag changes across all services.
ledger-db is a shared PostgreSQL datastore (no 'ledger-service' exists) with four DB writers: order-service, portfolio-service, payment-service and settlement-service.

The degradation is disk/WAL-capacity bound, not compute- or connection-bound: ledger-db cpu_pct was flat ~30% (min 25.73, max 32.79) across the window and connections_active stayed flat ~61-63, while replication_lag_ms climbed steadily 2468.37ms (13:00Z) to 5226.72ms (16:45Z) alongside the fill ramp.

There is an exact precedent for this mechanism: HIST-114 (2025-04-18, ledger-db) 'disk full from retained WAL', symptoms 'no space left on device'/'write failures', root cause 'Inactive replication slot retained WAL until disk filled', resolution 'Dropped slot; added slot-lag alert'.

payment-service error rate jumped from ~0.2-0.28% to 61.52% between the 14:55 and 15:00 buckets, sustaining ~58-64% through 16:55Z, with no traffic surge: request_rate stayed flat ~90-110 req/s (mean 100.11).

The blast radius is not uniform across ledger-db writers: portfolio-service stayed at ~0.15-0.27% error rate for the entire window with flat request_rate (mean 569.94 req/s) and flat db_pool_in_use (mean 11.97), and produced only one unrelated WARN (a connection-reset retry at 15:19:46Z).
settlement-service returned zero WARN+ logs in 14:45-16:59Z and zero in a widened 11:00-16:59Z query, so its ~54-55.8% error rate is not explained by any emitted error log.

The analytics_cdc slot's consumer is not a modeled, monitored component: get_service_dependencies returned not_found for 'analytics_cdc', 'analytics-service' and 'cdc-consumer', the known_services list (18 services) contains no analytics/CDC/consumer node, and the ledger-db dependency map lists only the four DB writers plus api-gateway HTTP callers.

assumptions: ASSUMPTION (from H2): The retained WAL from the inactive 'analytics_cdc' slot is the dominant space consumer. The fill ramp is measured (F19/F20) and matches the WAL-retention WARNs (F11), but no metric exposes WAL bytes or free bytes, so the causal direction (consumer stalled -> WAL retained -> disk fill) versus (something else filled the disk while the slot warning was incidental) remains an inference supported mainly by the exact HIST-114 precedent (F35).

ASSUMPTION (from H2): settlement-service fails via the same disk-exhaustion mechanism. Its ~54-56% error rate is VERIFIED (F14/F23) but it emitted zero WARN+ logs in both 14:45-16:59Z and 11:00-16:59Z (F27), so its error signature is genuinely unknown and the shared-mechanism attribution is inferred from it being a co-writer of the same disk-full datastore.

ASSUMPTION (from H2): The slot's consumer stall began before 14:16:25Z. The consumer is unmodeled (not in topology, no telemetry, F33/F34), so its stall time cannot be pinned; the direction of causality is asserted from the HIST-114 precedent, not observed.

ASSUMPTION: The reason order-service and settlement-service degraded while portfolio-service did not is that portfolio-service never reached the disk-write failure path in this window; the exact write-path difference (tables, read/write mix, caching) could not be determined from available data.

ASSUMPTION: No relevant change hides outside the recorded change set for modeled services. The 12-day deployment query returns only dep-6203 and the config-change query returns count 0 (F31/F32), but the unmodeled CDC consumer's deployment/config history is invisible to those tools.

(demoted from facts: no verified observation backs it) A likely space consumer on ledger-db is an inactive replication slot: WARN "replication slot 'analytics_cdc' is inactive; retaining 78423 MB of WAL" recurs from 14:16:25Z onward (5 occurrences).

timeline.event: ledger-db disk_used_pct measured at 89.39%; replication_lag_ms already 2468.37ms. Steady fill begins.
ledger-db disk crosses >95% (per the 14:05-14:10Z ramp), ~42 minutes before the v6.0.0 deploy.
ledger-db WARN "replication slot 'analytics_cdc' is inactive; retaining 78423 MB of WAL" first appears and recurs (5 occurrences).
ledger-db disk at 98%+ (>=98% from this bucket onward).
payment-service v6.0.0 (dep-6203, 'New UPI mandate flow', new ledger entry type MANDATE_HOLD) deployed by p.nair — the only change across all services in the incident window.
order-service and settlement-service 5xx spike begins in the 14:54Z bucket (16.17% avg / 49.57% max and 18.07% avg / 54.52% max respectively) — two writers that never received v6.0.0.
ledger-db disk_used_pct first reaches 100.0% and stays pinned at 100% through the end of data.
payment-service error_rate jumps from ~0.2-0.28% to 61.52% (in the 14:55->15:00 metric buckets) with flat request rate ~90-110 req/s.
payment-service first 'ledger write failed: ERROR: could not extend file: No space left on device' (88 of 89 WARN+ lines).
order-service first 'INSERT INTO orders failed: No space left on device' (236 occurrences through 16:57:47Z).
ledger-db PANIC 'could not write to file "pg_wal/xlogtemp...": No space left on device' (153 occurrences); 15:01:39Z data-file extension failure (139 occurrences).
dep-6203 rolled back — the last chance for a deployment-correlated recovery.

No recovery in any writer: payment-service 58-70% (mean 62.22), order-service ~47-50% (mean 47.89), settlement-service 53-58% (mean 54.92), all simultaneous through end of data; ledger-db disk remains 100%.
portfolio-service logs a single WARN (connection-reset retry); it never enters the disk-failure path and stays ~0.2% error rate all window.
ledger-db replication_lag_ms reaches 5226.72ms (from 2468.37ms at 13:00Z), tracking the disk ramp; cpu_pct and connections_active remain flat.

recommended_actions.action: Free space on ledger-db immediately by dropping the inactive replication slot 'analytics_cdc' (the exact HIST-114 resolution), or, if the slot must be preserved, restart/repoint its consumer and/or provision additional volume so WAL can be reclaimed and PostgreSQL can write WAL and extend data files again.
recommended_actions.rationale: ledger-db is pinned at 100% disk (F19) with PANIC on pg_wal and data-file extension (F10) and an inactive slot holding ~78 GB of WAL (F11); this is the only action that addresses the observed failure mechanism and matches the documented fix for the identical prior incident (F35).

recommended_actions.action: After freeing space, confirm recovery on the write-failure path: verify ledger-db disk_used_pct drops below 100% and that payment-service, order-service and settlement-service error rates fall back toward their pre-incident ~0.2% baseline.
recommended_actions.rationale: The one untested half of the discriminator is 'do services recover once disk is freed' — data ends with disk still at 100% and all three writers still elevated (F19, F21, F22, F23). Recovery on disk-free would close the loop on the shared-capacity root cause.

recommended_actions.action: Do not roll back or re-roll payment-service v6.0.0 as the remediation: keep dep-6203's rollback state as-is pending the disk fix, and treat the mandate flow as exonerated unless a validation-error signature appears.
recommended_actions.rationale: The 15:12Z rollback produced no recovery in any writer through 16:57Z (F21-F23) and the dominant error is ENOSPC (F8), also seen in a writer that never received v6.0.0 (F25); further rollback churn is unbounded risk with no expected benefit.

recommended_actions.action: Add alerting and automation for replication-slot retention: a slot-lag / retained-WAL-bytes alert and automatic paging when any slot is inactive beyond a threshold — the same mitigation recorded for HIST-114.
recommended_actions.rationale: The slot held ~78 GB of WAL with only a recurring WARN from 14:16:25Z (F11); the precedent incident's resolution was 'Dropped slot; added slot-lag alert' (F35). This converts a silent capacity leak into a pageable signal.

recommended_actions.action: Expose ledger-db capacity telemetry that currently does not exist: per-slot retained WAL bytes, free disk bytes, and WAL directory size, plus a disk-free alert well before 95% (e.g. 80%/90%).
recommended_actions.rationale: ledger-db exposes only connections_active, cpu_pct, disk_used_pct, replication_lag_ms, slow_queries_per_min (F12), so the space consumer can only be inferred from logs (F11); the fill ramp reached >95% by 14:05-14:10Z (F20) before anyone had a signal.

recommended_actions.action: Instrument or formally register the analytics_cdc slot consumer as a monitored component with its own health/telemetry, and add a dependency edge to ledger-db, so a stalled consumer is detectable.
recommended_actions.rationale: The consumer is absent from the topology: not_found for 'analytics_cdc'/'analytics-service'/'cdc-consumer' and no edge in the ledger-db dependency map (F33, F34), so its stall could not be timed or attributed.

recommended_actions.action: Fix cross-writer observability: ensure order-service, settlement-service and portfolio-service emit their DB write-failure errors with a consistent, queryable signature, and that log queries are not substring-biased (the 'ledger' filter missed 'INSERT INTO orders failed: No space left on device').
recommended_actions.rationale: The 'zero ledger matches' result was a substring artifact for order-service (F30) and settlement-service returned zero WARN+ logs of any kind despite ~54-55.8% errors (F27), delaying blast-radius confirmation.

recommended_actions.action: Review the shared-writer blast radius: run a capacity- and write-path review of all four ledger-db writers to explain why order-service/settlement-service failed while portfolio-service stayed healthy, and document the per-writer failure modes.
recommended_actions.rationale: The selective blast radius (F15, F28, F29) is the one unresolved explanatory gap in the shared-capacity story and affects future impact estimation.

recommended_actions.action: Prevent recurrence structurally: cap WAL retention per slot (max_slot_wal_keep_size) or set an automatic slot-drop/retention policy for ledger-db, and add disk-capacity runbook steps and a pre-flight capacity check for the shared datastore.
recommended_actions.rationale: This is the second ledger-db disk-full-from-retained-WAL incident (F35, F6); a retention cap plus runbook would prevent an inactive slot from ever filling the volume again.

recommended_actions.action: Until the mechanism is fully closed, verify the settlement-service alternative: since it shows ~54-55.8% errors with zero WARN+ logs (F27), check whether it fails on the same disk-write path or an independent mechanism once ledger-db capacity is restored.
recommended_actions.rationale: settlement-service is a verified degraded co-writer (F14, F23) but has no observable error signature; if it does not recover with the disk fix, a second mechanism must be investigated.

data_gaps: No metric for WAL volume, replication-slot retained bytes, or free disk bytes exists on ledger-db (only connections_active, cpu_pct, disk_used_pct, replication_lag_ms, slow_queries_per_min), so the exact space consumer (WAL from the inactive 'analytics_cdc' slot, per F11) can only be inferred from logs and the HIST-114 precedent, not confirmed from a metric series.

The analytics_cdc slot's consumer is unmodeled: get_service_dependencies returned not_found for 'analytics_cdc', 'analytics-service' and 'cdc-consumer', the known_services list contains no analytics/CDC node, and the ledger-db dependency map has no such edge (F33, F34). Its stall time and whether it was reconfigured around 14:15Z cannot be determined, so the causal direction (consumer stalled -> WAL retained -> disk fill) versus (something else filled the disk) cannot be separated by these tools.

No consumer-specific metric or per-slot lag/consumer-status metric is available, so the exact start of the WAL retention (as distinct from the 14:16:25Z warning threshold crossing) cannot be quantified.

settlement-service emitted zero WARN+ logs in 14:45-16:59Z and in a widened 11:00-16:59Z query despite a verified ~54-55.8% error rate (F14/F23/F27); its error signature is unknown, so the shared disk signature cannot be confirmed for the second of three degraded writers.

No data point exists after 16:57Z and ledger-db disk remains 100% through the last bucket, so 'do services recover once disk is freed' — the second half of the discriminator — is unanswerable; only the 'no rollback-correlated recovery' half is proven (F21-F23).

portfolio-service did not degrade despite writing to the same ledger-db (F15, F28, F29); the reason (read-only vs write path, caching, different tables) could not be determined, weakening a clean 'shared component down = all writers fail' statement.

The 12-day config-change query returns count 0 across all services (F31) and only one deployment (F32), but these tools cover modeled services only; any deployment or config change to the unmodeled CDC consumer is invisible.
Historical incidents are recorded as leads only and not evidence for this incident (F6, F35, F36); no incident record exists of the analytics_cdc consumer being stopped or reconfigured.
what_would_change_the_conclusion: A measurement showing ledger-db free disk / WAL bytes never actually depleted (i.e. disk_used_pct was misreported and the volume had free space) would undercut the disk-exhaustion mechanism, since the fill ramp is the load-bearing observation (F19/F20).

Evidence that a writer hit the same failure while ledger-db was below full (before ~14:58Z), or that failures appear in sources unrelated to ledger-db writes, would break the shared-capacity causal chain.

Demonstration that a ledger-side schema/config change (e.g. a CHECK constraint on entry_type) or a mandate-specific validation error exists — e.g. WARN+ logs on payment-service containing a MANDATE_HOLD / unknown-entry-type rejection — would revive H1/H3 and contradict the ENOSPC-only signature (F8).

Finding that the volume was not filled by WAL, but by another consumer (e.g. log retention, a batch job, an unrecorded config change), would move the trigger identity away from the inactive replication slot while leaving the capacity root cause — i.e. it would shift H2's mechanism to H4's unnamed trigger.

Recovery of payment-service, order-service and settlement-service errors to baseline only after a deployment-level revert (as opposed to after freeing ledger-db disk) would point back toward a change-induced cause and overturn the coincidental-deployment conclusion.
Proof that settlement-service's ~54-55.8% errors arise from an independent mechanism unaffected by ledger-db capacity would reduce H2's scope and reopen a second, unexplained fault.

findings.statement: The ONLY change in the incident window 2026-06-01T13:00Z-16:59Z across ALL services is payment-service v6.0.0 (dep-6203), deployed 2026-06-01T14:46:00Z by p.nair, summary 'New UPI mandate flow', changes include 'new ledger entry type MANDATE_HOLD', status rolled_back at 2026-06-01T15:12:00Z. No other service deployed a change.

No config/flag changes were recorded in the window. A first query for config changes returned count 0 for all services; the wider confirmation query (2026-05-20 onward) hit the tool-call budget and did not run.

There is NO 'ledger-service' in the system; the ledger is a SHARED postgres datastore 'ledger-db' (owner platform, shared:true, has_telemetry:true). Queries for a 'ledger-service' returned not_found in both dependency and deployment tools.

payment-service writes directly to the shared ledger-db (edge 'payment-service' -> 'ledger-db' kind 'db') and also produces to the shared kafka queue. ledger-db is shared by four writers: order-service, portfolio-service, payment-service, settlement-service all have db edges into ledger-db.

Dependency graph shows no dedicated schema-validation service between payment-service and ledger-db; the ledger entry type MANDATE_HOLD validation (if any) would have to live in payment-service itself or in ledger-db schema/constraints. payment-service's other edges are bank-partner-api (external, no telemetry) and kafka (queue-produce).

Historical incidents on ledger-db are all different root causes from a 'new entry type' break: HIST-114 disk full from retained WAL (write failures, resource_exhaustion), HIST-111 unindexed report scan (bad_deployment), HIST-110 IOPS throttling, HIST-102 failover. No prior incident mentions an invalid/unknown ledger entry type -- these are leads only, not evidence.

findings.statement: There is no service named 'ledger-service' or 'ledger service'; the ledger datastore is 'ledger-db' (PostgreSQL). Both log and metric queries for ledger-service returned unknown-service errors.

ledger-db disk exhaustion preceded the payment errors: WARN 'disk usage 95%' at 14:15:45Z and 'disk usage 98%' at 14:48:20Z, followed by hard write failures 'PANIC: could not write to file "pg_wal/xlogtemp...": No space left on device' first at 15:01:01Z (153 occurrences) and 'could not extend file "base/16402/2619": No space left on device' first at 15:01:39Z (139 occurrences).

findings.statement: ledger-db CPU was flat at ~30% across the whole window (min 25.73, max 32.79, mean 29.98), i.e. no CPU saturation coincident with onset -- the degradation is disk/WAL capacity, not compute load. ledger-db exposes only connections_active, cpu_pct, disk_used_pct, replication_lag_ms, slow_queries_per_min.

order-service (a ledger-db writer that did NOT get v6.0.0) error rate was flat ~0.2-0.23% through the 14:45Z bucket, then jumped to 16.17% avg / 49.57% max in the 14:54Z bucket and held ~47-48% (max ~51.8%) through 16:51Z. Failures are therefore NOT confined to payment-service/mandate path.
settlement-service (another non-v6.0.0 ledger-db writer) shows the identical pattern: flat ~0.17-0.22% through 14:45Z, then 18.07% avg / 54.52% max at 14:54Z, holding ~54-55.8% through 16:51Z.

portfolio-service error rate stayed flat at ~0.15-0.27% across the ENTIRE window (14:00Z-16:51Z), showing the shared-db blast radius is NOT uniform across all ledger-db writers — order and settlement degraded, portfolio did not.

No WARN+ log line from order-service, settlement-service, or portfolio-service matched the substring 'ledger' in 14:00-16:59Z (total_matched 0 for each). The write-failure logs are not surfaced from these writers, even though two of them show 48-55% error rates — so log-based blast radius undercounts non-payment writers.

The onset ordering on the shared component precedes the v6.0.0 rollout: v6.0.0 deployed 14:46Z (dep-6203), but ledger-db was already at 'disk usage 95%' by 14:15:45Z and 'disk usage 98%' by 14:48:20Z, and order-service/settlement-service 5xx spike begins in the 14:54Z bucket — i.e. degradation started before/at the completion of the rollout, not only after mandate traffic hit the ledger. This favours a shared-component failure over a new-entry-type rejection.
payment-service request rate stayed flat (~90-110 req/s, mean 100.11) across 14:00-16:56Z with no traffic surge at rollout; so the error-rate jump is not load-driven on payment-service.

ledger-db disk_used_pct is the correct metric name; it rises monotonically from 89.39% (13:00Z) to 99.92%/100% by the 14:55Z bucket, then pins at exactly 'avg':100.0,'max':100 for every bucket from 15:00Z through 16:55Z (missing_points 0). No recovery or cleanup ever occurs.

The disk fill ramp crosses critical thresholds well before the v6.0.0 rollout completed: >95% by 14:05-14:10Z, 98%+ from the 14:38Z bucket, 99.28% at 14:48:20-ish (14:48 bucket), and 100.0% first reached in the 14:58Z bucket — i.e. the volume was at ~98% when v6.0.0 deployed at 14:46Z and full ~12 min later.

DECISIVE NEGATIVE: payment-service error_rate does NOT recover after the 15:12Z rollback. It sits at 61.68% at 15:12Z and stays in the 58-70% band continuously through 16:57Z (avg 61.51, max 63.76 in the final bucket; mean 62.22 across the window, min 55.31, max 70.45).

order-service error_rate is likewise persisted, not recovering: ~47-50% from 15:00Z (47.99 avg / 49.57 max) through 16:57Z (46.93 / 46.98); mean 47.89 over 15:00-17:00Z. It never drops back to the pre-incident ~0.2%.

settlement-service error_rate is persisted as well: 53-58% throughout 15:00-17:00Z (54.52 max at 15:00Z, 55.88 avg at 16:57Z), mean 54.92, min 50.67. All three writers remain elevated simultaneously at the end of data — no service-specific recovery separates payment-service from the other two.

Other ledger-db metrics corroborate a space/IO-bound (not compute- or connection-bound) shared component: replication_lag_ms climbs steadily 2468.37ms (13:00Z) -> 5226.72ms (16:45Z) matching the fill ramp, while connections_active stays flat ~61-63 (mean 62.26, max 68.34) and earlier cpu_pct was flat ~30% (F12). The lag ramp and disk ramp move together and neither recovers.

order-service, a ledger-db writer that did NOT receive v6.0.0, emits the same no-space-of-device disk-write failure signature as payment-service. In 14:45-16:59Z it had total_matched 238 WARN+ logs (236 ERROR, 2 WARN), dominated by the pattern 'INSERT INTO orders failed: No space left on device' (count 236, first_seen 2026-06-01T15:00:42Z, last_match 16:57:47Z). This confirms the failure is a shared storage-exhaustion mechanism, not the payment-service 'unknown ledger entry type' path.

findings.statement: The order-service disk-failure onset (15:00:42Z first ERROR) sits ~15 minutes after the v6.0.0 deploy (14:46Z) but coincides with payment-service's first 'ledger write failed ... No space left on device' at 15:00:26Z (F8) and ledger-db's hard write failures at 15:01:01Z (F10) — i.e. the writers break in the same minute, consistent with one shared component crossing the ENOSPC threshold rather than each writer's own change.

settlement-service is the one degraded writer whose logs do NOT carry the signature: an unfiltered WARN+ query for 14:45-16:59Z returned total_matched 0 (no ERROR, no WARN), and widening the window back to 11:00Z also returned total_matched 0 over an explicitly reported data_range 11:00Z-16:59Z. So despite its ~54-55.8% error rate (F14), no log evidence of any error mechanism exists for settlement-service in this window.

portfolio-service, the flat ~0.2% counterexample (F15), produced exactly ONE WARN+ log in 14:45-16:59Z: a single WARN at 15:19:46Z 'retrying idempotent request (attempt 2) after connection reset'. That is a transient connection-reset retry, NOT a no-space/disk-write failure — so portfolio-service's low error rate reflects that it never hit the disk-exhaustion failure path in this window, not a different error that was merely undercounted.

refs.quote: retrying idempotent request (attempt 2) after connection reset

findings.statement: portfolio-service's DB usage shows no sign of stress during the incident: request_rate was flat (mean 569.94 req/s, min 505.55, max 625.27, missing_points 0) and its db_pool_in_use was flat at mean 11.97 connections (min 10.58, max 13.05) across 14:00-16:59Z. Its healthy error rate is therefore accompanied by normal traffic and normal DB connection usage — not a writer that was starved or saturated.

The shared-signature claim (F16 had zero 'ledger' matches for these writers) is now RESOLVED for order-service: it was a substring artifact, not absence. order-service DOES emit the shared disk-failure signature, but with 'INSERT INTO orders' wording rather than the word 'ledger'. The claim still cannot be confirmed for settlement-service (zero WARN+ lines of any kind) and is not applicable to portfolio-service (one unrelated retry log).

findings.statement: The previously-unrun F2 config/change query over 2026-05-20T00:00Z to 2026-06-01T17:00Z now executed and returned count 0 config/feature-flag changes across ALL services. So H4's 'another config change is the trigger' branch has no config-change candidate anywhere in the 12-day window.

The same long-window deployment query (2026-05-20 to 2026-06-01) returns exactly one deployment: dep-6203 payment-service v6.0.0 at 2026-06-01T14:46:00Z, status rolled_back. No deployment of ledger-db or any CDC/analytics component appears in the entire 12-day lookback.

No component named for the analytics_cdc slot's consumer exists in the topology: get_service_dependencies returned not_found for 'analytics_cdc', 'analytics-service' and 'cdc-consumer', and the tool's known_services list (18 services) contains no analytics/CDC/consumer node at all. The dependent consuming the slot is not a modeled, monitored service.

The ledger-db dependency map (depth 2, both directions) lists only the four DB writers (order-, portfolio-, payment-, settlement-service) plus api-gateway HTTP callers; there is no edge to any analytics/CDC consumer. So I cannot attribute the slot's inactivity to a dependency-graph-visible consumer failure or reconfiguration.

findings.statement: There IS an exact precedent for H2's mechanism: HIST-114 (2025-04-18, ledger-db) 'disk full from retained WAL', symptoms 'no space left on device','write failures', root_cause 'Inactive replication slot retained WAL until disk filled', category resource_exhaustion, resolution 'Dropped slot; added slot-lag alert'. This is a lead only, not evidence about this incident, but it matches F11's analytics_cdc slot WAL retention exactly.
